title: Introduce local live-indexing dev proxy + browser sync quickstart
author: Lena Park
description:
Motivation: developer feedback loops for RAG workflows are bottlenecked by slow index refreshes and heavyweight local indexing steps. This quickstart introduces a small dev proxy + browser sync pattern that lets authors iterate on indexing, retrieval prompts, and agent tool bindings without rebuilding the entire index.

Summary: Add a lightweight 'live-index-proxy' quickstart that runs a local devserver which accepts document diffs, applies incremental updates to an in-memory index (with optional persistent snapshot), and broadcasts index updates to instrumented browser playbacks via WebSocket. The pattern enables: 1) incremental index syncs from local files or external connectors; 2) immediate replay in a browser-based RAG playground; 3) deterministic test harness hooks for e2e smoke tests and telemetry probes.

What this PR includes: checklist and deliverables: 
- [x] Quickstart README with step-by-step local setup and troubleshooting tips (port conflicts, KMS hints).
- [x] TypeScript devserver (devserver.ts) implementing a pluggable connector interface (filewatch, sample-csv, mocked-s3).
- [x] Browser sync artifacts (indexer-worker.js, playground index.html) that connect to the proxy and maintain a small in-memory tokenized store for retrieval demos.
- [x] Example RAG agent tool binding showing how the client-side can switch between local live index and remote embeddings service.
- [x] Lightweight telemetry probes (opt-in) and a sample tracing span emitted during incremental apply.
- [x] Unit tests for connector glue and an e2e smoke script that runs the devserver + headless chrome playback.

Usage notes: The quickstart is intentionally conservative — the in-memory index is not for production. The goal is rapid iteration and reproducible dev scenarios. The README has explicit steps to swap to a real embeddings backend for performance testing.

Related: ENG-3211 (dev loop perf), PM-87 (RAG authoring product goal), SUP-1423 (support case that motivated local S3 mock).

Release notes: Adds a new local developer quickstart: 'live-index-proxy' that enables incremental indexing + browser replay for RAG authoring. Not a breaking change.

Testing & CI: local unit tests and an e2e smoke script were added. CI runs for this PR included lint, unit, and an optional headless-e2e job. The headless job is marked allowed-to-fail on CI to reduce flakiness; we still run it manually as part of release verification.

diff_snippets: devserver.ts: added WebSocket-based update broadcast and minimal 'applyDiff' that handles add/update/delete ops (approx. 120 LOC)

review_comments: Samir Shah (2026-02-22): Nice pattern. Can we make the connector interface smaller so it is easier to stub in tests? Suggest removing optional lifecycle hooks and consolidate to applyChanges(diffs).
Lena Park (2026-02-22): Responded: agree, slimmed interface to applyChanges + snapshot API. Left lifecycle hooks for future when we wire long-running connectors (commented in code).

Claire Nguyen (2026-02-24): Found a concurrency race when two diffs for the same doc ID arrive quickly; added suggestion to use a per-doc mutex and included a reference to a small helper in utils/locks.ts.
Lena Park (2026-02-25): Fixed in second commit — added strict ordering and a per-doc queue. Updated tests to simulate quick successive diffs.

Tomás Rivera (2026-02-26): CI headless-e2e flaky on macOS runners; recommend marking job as allowed-to-fail in main workflow and adding local instructions for manual verification. Approved after tests passed on Linux runners.
ci_checks: headless-e2e (allowed-to-fail): flaky -> rerun passed on linux
release_notes: Add 'live-index-proxy' quickstart: local devserver + browser sync for incremental RAG indexing and replay. Intended for developer workflows; not for production indexing.
notes_for_maintainers: This quickstart intentionally leaves the connector interface lightweight; if we later add more persistent snapshots (sqlite/rocksdb), move implementations under quickstarts/live-index-proxy/backends. The headless-e2e job is allowed-to-fail to avoid CI noise; maintainers should run it manually when validating release branches.
manual_verification_steps: 1) yarn install && yarn build in quickstarts/live-index-proxy
3) open quickstarts/live-index-proxy/examples/playground/index.html (or run yarn test:e2e) and create a small doc set
4) modify a watched file and confirm browser playground reflects the change within 1s
5) run the sample RAG agent in examples and toggle between local and remote embeddings backends to validate retrieval responses
